| [QUESTION-072](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-072.md) v5 | Does a project memory distribute credibility among an argument's contributors, by making some contributors' moves addressable and leaving others' as unfiled turns, so that what gets a code gets cited and what does not is re-derived or lost? | Filed at the owner's request, ahead of its readings: Fricker's account of testimonial and hermeneutical injustice ([LIT-1004](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1004.md)) is registered unread in the same contribution. [CLAIM-182](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-182.md) says addressability is what makes an anchor, and [CLAIM-181](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-181.md) says the record's grammar decides what can be filed. Together they imply that a contributor whose moves are filed gains standing in the argument that one whose moves are not does not. | [QUESTION-366](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-366.md) v2 | Does an inquiry need the record of its own development to know its object, as Simondon's method and its organization-studies readers hold, or only to revise its conclusions, which is what the record has shown? | Bencherki, Brummans and Vézy (2024, p. 1366), quoting Simondon, hold that research "consists in following the being in its genesis, in accomplishing the genesis of thought at the same time as the genesis of the object", and Bencherki and Iliadis (proposition 4) that knowledge of an entity "should reflect on the way that knowledge itself has individuated". The record has shown a narrower thing: an inquiry's history is needed to fix its revisions ([CLAIM-294](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-294.md)), and a stabilized specification lets later inquiry proceed without repeating the history that made it ([CLAIM-475](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-475.md)). Whether the history is needed for anything besides revision is open, and an answer would also say whether the record's objects are constituted by its inquiry in any sense beyond [CLAIM-469](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-469.md)'s operational one, which is [CLAIM-476](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-476.md)'s unanswered defeater. | Open |
